title.en: Functions in SQL and GROUP BY
title.kn: SQL ನಲ್ಲಿ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು GROUP BY

hook.en: The principal does not want 600 rows. She wants the class average, the topper's marks, and how many students came from each city. SQL functions and GROUP BY give these in one query.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರಾಂಶುಪಾಲರಿಗೆ 600 ಸಾಲುಗಳು ಬೇಡ. ತರಗತಿ ಸರಾಸರಿ, ಅತ್ಯಧಿಕ ಅಂಕ, ಪ್ರತಿ ನಗರದಿಂದ ಎಷ್ಟು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಎಂಬುದು ಬೇಕು. SQL ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು GROUP BY ಇದನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Group rows with GROUP BY and filter groups with HAVING

narration.en: The principal does not want 600 rows. She wants the class average, the topper's marks, and how many students came from each city. SQL functions and GROUP BY give these in one query.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರಾಂಶುಪಾಲರಿಗೆ 600 ಸಾಲುಗಳು ಬೇಡ. ತರಗತಿ ಸರಾಸರಿ, ಅತ್ಯಧಿಕ ಅಂಕ, ಪ್ರತಿ ನಗರದಿಂದ ಎಷ್ಟು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಎಂಬುದು ಬೇಕು. SQL ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು GROUP BY ಇದನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Single-row functions work on each row and return one value per row. Math: POWER(x, y), ROUND(n, d), MOD(a, b). String: UCASE/UPPER, LCASE/LOWER, LENGTH, LEFT, RIGHT, MID/SUBSTRING (SUBSTR in SQLite), INSTR, LTRIM, RTRIM, TRIM. Date (MySQL): NOW(), DATE(), MONTH(), MONTHNAME(), YEAR(), DAY(), DAYNAME().

points.en: String: UPPER, LOWER, LENGTH, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, INSTR, TRIM
Date: NOW, DATE, MONTH, YEAR, DAY, DAYNAME

narration.en: Single-row functions give one answer for every row: math functions like ROUND, string functions like UPPER and LENGTH, and date functions like YEAR.
narration.kn: ಏಕ-ಸಾಲು ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಾಲಿಗೆ ಒಂದು ಉತ್ತರ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ: ROUND ನಂತಹ ಗಣಿತ, UPPER, LENGTH ನಂತಹ ಸ್ಟ್ರಿಂಗ್, YEAR ನಂತಹ ದಿನಾಂಕ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು.

title.en: On the board: GROUP BY: one result per group

say.en: GROUP BY Class collects the rows with the same class into one group.
For 12A, COUNT of star counts all 3 rows, but COUNT of Marks and AVG ignore the NULL. AVG is 85 plus 91 over 2, which is 88.
For 12B, COUNT is 2 and AVG is 72 plus 64 over 2, which is 68.
HAVING filters groups after grouping: HAVING AVG of Marks greater than 80 keeps only 12A.

narration.en: We group the STUDENT rows by class and compute COUNT and AVG for each group, noticing how NULL is treated.

body.en: Aggregate (multiple-row) functions work on a set of rows and return one value: MAX, MIN, AVG, SUM, COUNT. They ignore NULL values, except COUNT(*), which counts all rows. GROUP BY column forms groups of rows with the same value, and the aggregate is computed for each group. HAVING filters groups; WHERE filters rows before grouping.

points.en: COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(col) skips NULL
WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups

narration.en: Aggregate functions like SUM, AVG and COUNT summarise many rows into one value. GROUP BY makes groups, and HAVING filters those groups.
narration.kn: SUM, AVG, COUNT ನಂತಹ ಸಮೂಹ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಹಲವು ಸಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಒಂದು ಮೌಲ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಕ್ಷೇಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. GROUP BY ಗುಂಪು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, HAVING ಗುಂಪುಗಳನ್ನು ಸೋಸುತ್ತದೆ.

caption.en: Change the marks of four students and watch SUM, AVG, MAX and MIN, the aggregate functions of SQL.

tryThis.en: Set all four equal: what are AVG, MAX and MIN?
Raise only the highest mark: which aggregates change?
If one mark were NULL, how would AVG be calculated in SQL?

narration.en: Change the marks of four students and watch SUM, AVG, MAX and MIN, the aggregate functions of SQL. Set all four equal: what are AVG, MAX and MIN?

problem.en: Table STUDENT(RollNo, SName, Gender, City, Marks) has 6 rows: (1, Asha, F, Mysuru, 85), (2, Ravi, M, Hubballi, 72), (3, Meena, F, Mysuru, 91), (4, Kiran, M, Mangaluru, NULL), (5, Arjun, M, Mysuru, 64), (6, Divya, F, Hubballi, 78). Find COUNT(*), COUNT(Marks), AVG(Marks), MAX(Marks) and SUM(Marks).

steps.en: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(Marks), AVG(Marks), MAX(Marks), SUM(Marks) FROM STUDENT;
COUNT(*) = 6 rows; COUNT(Marks) = 5 because Kiran's marks are NULL.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Table STUDENT(RollNo, SName, Gender, City, Marks) has 6 rows: (1, Asha, F, Mysuru, 85), (2, Ravi, M, Hubballi, 72), (3, Meena, F, Mysuru, 91), (4, Kiran, M, Mangaluru, NULL), (5, Arjun, M, Mysuru, 64), (6, Divya, F, Hubballi, 78). Find COUNT(*), COUNT(Marks), AVG(Marks), MAX(Marks) and SUM(Marks).

problem.en: Using the same table, find the number of students and average marks city-wise, showing only cities with more than one student.

steps.en: SELECT City, COUNT(*), AVG(Marks) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY City HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
Mysuru: Asha 85, Meena 91, Arjun 64 → 3 students, average 240 / 3 = 80.
Mangaluru has only 1 student, so HAVING removes it.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Using the same table, find the number of students and average marks city-wise, showing only cities with more than one student.

homework.en: Write a query to show the highest marks for each gender in STUDENT and predict its output.

narration.en: Recap. Single-row functions return one value per row. Aggregates (MAX, MIN, AVG, SUM, COUNT) return one value for many rows. Aggregates ignore NULL, except COUNT(*). GROUP BY makes groups; HAVING filters groups.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಏಕ-ಸಾಲು ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಾಲಿಗೆ ಒಂದು ಮೌಲ್ಯ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಸಮೂಹ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಹಲವು ಸಾಲುಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಂದು ಮೌಲ್ಯ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. COUNT(*) ಹೊರತು ಸಮೂಹ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು NULL ಅನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. GROUP BY ಗುಂಪು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; HAVING ಗುಂಪುಗಳನ್ನು ಸೋಸುತ್ತದೆ.
